rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 3-6 describe the author's own prototype (Arduino, HL-69 soil hygrometer, DHT22, BH1750 light, SEN0169 pH sensor, GSM module), own training dataset (Tables 1-3) and own KNN performance tests (Tables 5-7, Fig. 11).
rows.notes: The study's system does not monitor electrical conductivity at all; it uses a pH sensor, soil moisture, air humidity/temperature, light and weather forecast data. No salinity, EC or soil-health variable is measured or reported. The only quantitative results are KNN classification metrics (error vs k, precision/recall/F1, a 98.6% recognition rate and RMSE 0.1 compared with ref. [21]). Claims about preventing over-irrigation or mitigating salinity are not supported by any field measurement; the statement that the prototype reduces water use is asserted without data.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 4 and 6 report the author's own hardware prototype, training dataset and KNN classifier evaluation (Tables 5-7, Fig. 11).
rows.notes: No crop yield, growth, quality or productivity data are collected or reported; crop type enters only as ontology background (rice > sugarcane > maize > cotton > wheat water need, Table 3). 'Increased crop yield productivity' is listed in 6.6 as a key benefit without any measurement. EC/salinity is not monitored. Results are limited to classifier accuracy metrics.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 4 and 6 report the author's own IoT prototype deployed in a field, own dataset (Tables 1-3) and own KNN performance analysis (Tables 5-7, Fig. 11).
rows.notes: The study builds a decision system that recommends irrigation need classes (HNN to HN) from soil moisture, humidity, temperature and weather forecast, and reports only classification performance (mean error vs k, precision/recall/F1, 98.6% accuracy, RMSE 0.1). No measurement of water applied, water saved or over-irrigation avoided is reported; the abstract/conclusion assertion that the prototype reduces water use is unsupported by any data in the paper (the rainy-day 20% example is a design rule, not a result). The system does not monitor EC. Treated as upstream: it supplies a scheduling decision, the precondition for water conservation, without measuring the effect.

notes: Full text appears complete (abstract through references). The paper is an engineering prototype/ML classifier paper: its only quantitative own results are KNN error rates and precision/recall/F1 tables compared with refs [15] and [21]. There is no EC sensor, no salinity data, no water-use measurement and no crop outcome data, so none of the three claim rows (EC monitoring, salinity mitigation, over-irrigation prevention) is supported by the study's own results. Some table characters (Table 3) are OCR-garbled but do not affect the rating.
